title: Aggregated results object
description: Written by the harness — one per backend. Each metric is summarized as [p50, max] over the appropriate sample pool.

host.description: Machine name — hostname, or `bench run --machine`. The analysis loader's label when results aren't under a per-machine subdir.

iters.description: K: in-process timed iterations per spawn (default 5).

spawns.description: S: process re-spawns per cell (default 3). Timing n = iters×spawns; load/mem n = spawns.

stat.description: [p50, max] — median ranks the stacks, max flags instability.

oneOf.description: Not measurable for this backend/provider (e.g. *_vram on a CPU EP).

unhealthy_reason.description: Present iff healthy=false: which brain-check failed and why; timed tasks were skipped.

timed_out_tasks.description: Timed tasks judged too slow to score: a single iteration outlived the harness backstop, or a smaller task ran below the usable tok/s floor (costlier tasks are then skipped). Absent from `tasks`; the report shows them as 'too slow'.

errored_tasks.description: Timed tasks that were attempted but produced no sample for a reason other than slowness — a spawn that died emitting nothing (crash, OOM, device-lost). Distinct from `timed_out_tasks`: a failure, not slowness. Absent from `tasks`; the report shows them as 'errored'.

vram_method.description: How per-PID VRAM was obtained: NVML, DRM fdinfo's device-local pool (a discrete card's VRAM, or an APU's BIOS carve-out — reserved before boot, so not host RAM), unified memory, or unavailable.

cold_start_ms.description: First-touch load (cold page cache): model-load + context-init, attributed once to the first scored task, n=1.

model_load_ms.description: Warm load phase — read/mmap weights and upload to the device. Warm spawns pooled.

context_init_ms.description: Warm load phase — allocate the KV cache / compute graph / context after weights are resident.

warmup_ms.description: Warm load phase — one-time kernel/JIT warm pass before the timed iterations. Paid once per process, before any prompt.

memory.description: Per-phase footprint over the timed iterations. Prefill is a ramp, so only its peak is meaningful. Decode is a plateau and gets two stats: *peak* (high-water — what the device must fit) and *sustained* (median over the decode samples — the steady per-token working set). They diverge when a transient rides into the decode window (e.g. a shape recompile spike still draining when decode starts).

prefill_rss_peak_mb.description: Peak (high-water) RSS over the prefill spans of the timed iterations — the prompt-ingestion working set. Null if no sample landed in a prefill batch (a prefill shorter than the ~10 ms sample cadence).

prefill_vram_peak_mb.description: Peak VRAM over the prefill spans; null on a CPU EP / unified memory or when no prefill sample landed.

decode_rss_peak_mb.description: Peak (high-water) RSS over the decode spans — what must fit in RAM. Null only if no sample landed in decode.

decode_vram_peak_mb.description: Peak VRAM over the decode spans; null on a CPU EP / unified memory or when no decode sample landed.

decode_rss_sustained_mb.description: Median RSS over the decode spans — the sustained generation working set (weights + KV + per-token activations), immune to transients draining out of prefill.

decode_vram_sustained_mb.description: Median VRAM over the decode spans; null on a CPU EP / unified memory or when no decode sample landed.

sample_completions.description: A few decoded completions (last turn) carried up from the events, so a human can eyeball that the stack produced real text, not garbage. Inspection aid only — not scored.
